51.0.0.en: 1 A prayer of Jesus the son of Sirach: I will give thanks unto You, O Lord and King, and praise You, O God my Savior. 2 I give thanks unto Your name, for You have been my defender and helper, 3 and have redeemed my body from destruction, and from the snare of the slanderous tongue, and from the lips of those that forge lies, and were my helper against those that withstood me, 4 and have delivered me, according to the multitude of Your mercies and of Your name, from the roaring of those prepared to devour. 5 Out of the hands of such as sought after my life, and from the many afflictions which I had; 6 from the choking of the fire on every side, and from the midst of the fire where I was not burned; 7 from the depth of the belly of hell, from an unclean tongue, and from lying words, and from the slander of an unrighteous tongue before the king. 8 My soul drew near unto death, 9 and my life was near to the depth of hell. 10 They compassed me on every side, and there was no man to help me. I looked for the succor of men, but there was none. 11 Then I remembered Your mercy, O Lord, and Your works of old: 12 how You deliver those that wait for You, and save them out of the hands of the nations. 13 Then I lifted up my prayer from the earth, and prayed for deliverance from death. 14 I called upon the Lord the Father of my Lord, that He would not leave me in the days of my trouble, in the time of the proud, when there was no help. 15 I will praise Your name continually, and will sing praise with thanksgiving, for my prayer was heard. 16 For You saved me from destruction, and delivered me from the evil time. 17 Therefore will I give thanks unto You, and praise You, and bless the name of the Lord.

51.0.1.en: If the book calls for fellowship in praise, on the other hand the believer must offer a hymn of thanksgiving for God's dealings with him personally, as Savior and King. This hymn, or this psalm, comes bearing the echo of many of the hymns found in the book of Psalms, especially the two psalms (Ps 120; 136).

51.0.2.en: This hymn came as a practical model of thanksgiving for deliverance from the plots of hidden and open enemies.

51.0.3.en: a. The desire to praise the Lord: Before Ben Sira sets out what befell him, he made clear at the beginning, as at the end, his earnest desire to praise God [1, 12], as though the believer, whether he enters into trials or does not, never ceases in his depths to give thanks to God. Rather, trials, however intense they become, kindle the heart still more to give thanks to God for His works with us in the midst of affliction.

51.1.0.en: b. Ben Sira's deliverance from certain death [2-6].

51.1.1.en: c. God's wondrous salvation: when a man feels isolated, with no helper to support him, the Lord reveals Himself in his life as King and Savior.

51.2.0.en: d. The Lord's response to the cries of his heart [10].

51.3.0.en: e. His setting out to praise [12].

51.3.1.en: I give thanks to You, O Lord the King, and I praise You, O God my Savior, and I give thanks to Your name [1].

51.3.2.en: Ben Sira revealed his longing to praise the Lord, his King and Savior. And in great brevity he enumerated the dangers that befell him and from which the Lord rescued him, for men had forsaken him, and he had drawn near to death; they had threatened him and wanted to devour him.

51.3.3.en: The secret of praise is the believer's realization of the truth about God, that He is the King of kings, the Ruler of all, and the Savior who loves all mankind. God, in His fatherhood to humanity, will not ignore the needs of any man, and in His work of salvation He is able to give us His divine righteousness in place of our sins and weaknesses.

51.3.4.en: For You are my fortress and my helper, and You have delivered my body from destruction, and from the snare of the slandering tongue, and from lying lips. And against those who withstood me You were my help, and You redeemed me [2].

51.3.5.en: He likens the tongue of the slanderer to the bites of a poisonous serpent, which fasten into a man's body and instill their deadly venom in it. God, in honoring man, gave him perfect freedom. But when he abuses what God has given, using his tongue for slander and his mouth for lying and setting snares for the righteous, God does not allow the rod of the sinners to rest upon the head of the righteous (Ps 125:3).

51.3.6.en: v God may sometimes permit the rod of sinners to strike the righteous, but He does not let this rod rest for a long time. What is the rod of sinners but their power, their dominion and their harm?

51.3.7.en: St. John Chrysostom: According to the greatness of Your mercy and Your name, from my being devoured as one prepared for eating, and from the hands of those who seek my soul, and from the many afflictions that I endured [3].

51.3.8.en: Some see that Sirach's song here points to his deliverance from a deadly danger because of false accusations that a man who opposed the truth brought against Ben Sira before one of the kings, and Ben Sira was on the point of being killed.

51.3.9.en: And from the choking of the flame which surrounded me on every side, and from the midst of the fire which I had not kindled [4].

51.3.10.en: Through the flame of the fire of an extremely cruel injustice all the doors of human help are closed, so that the Lord may open to us the door of His mercies, and we discover the depth of His love and perceive the wisdom of His ordering of our lives.

51.3.11.en: And from the depth of the womb of the abyss, and from the unclean tongue and the word of lying [5].

51.3.12.en: The slander of an unrighteous tongue before the king. My soul drew near to death, and my life approached the lowest part of the abyss [6].

51.3.13.en: Some see that an unknown person, or several persons, presented to King Antiochus III a report about Ben Sira that he was a traitor to the king.

51.3.14.en: They surrounded me on every side, and there was no helper. I looked for the help of men, and there was none [7].

51.3.15.en: I remembered Your mercy, O Lord, and Your work which is from of old, for You lift up those who wait for You, and save them from the hands of their enemies [8].

51.3.16.en: So I sent up my petition from the earth, and prayed concerning the turmoil that death causes [9].

51.3.17.en: When all the doors of men were shut in his face, he found in meeting with God, the Lover of mankind, the way of escape from the injustice of the wicked.

51.3.18.en: I called upon the Lord, the Father of my Lord, that He would not leave me in the days of trouble, when there is no help for me against the proud. I will praise Your name at all times, and sing to Him a hymn of thanksgiving [10].

51.3.19.en: His speech about God came as "the Lord, the Father of my Lord" [10]. Who is the Father of my Lord? This cannot be understood except in the light of the Christian thought concerning the hypostases of the Father and the Son.

51.3.20.en: Ben Sira presents to us a practical exercise for enjoying God's answer to our prayer, which is that we mix our cries in the midst of affliction with thanksgiving and praise to God. As Origen says, thanksgiving in the midst of affliction reveals our surrender and our trust in God, the Maker of good things. Thanksgiving in the time of relief cannot be compared with the greatness of thanksgiving in the time of affliction.

51.3.21.en: v Since danger accompanies the keeping of the commandment, which is our boast, let us remember the saying of the Apostle: "It were better for me to die, than that any man should make my glorying void" (1 Cor 9:15). And he says at greater length in another place: "Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?" (Rom 8:35). Here we learn, in a stronger expression, to obey the commandments, and how to show our intense love for God, who said: "If a man love me, he will keep my words" (Jn 14:23), and also in other places, so that rest may be poured into our souls...

51.3.22.en: From these verses it is clear that whoever transgresses even one commandment will be subject to the general judgment, since the Lord declared: "He that rejecteth me, and receiveth not my words, hath one that judgeth him: the word that I have spoken, the same shall judge him in the last day" (Jn 12:48). And the words that followed are more terrifying... (Jn 3:36)[1].

51.3.23.en: St. Basil the Great: My prayer was heard. For You saved me from destruction, and delivered me from the evil time [11].

51.3.24.en: Therefore I give thanks to You and praise You, and I bless the name of the Lord [12].

51.3.25.en: The psalm ends with praise as at the beginning, and in this it resembles (Psalm 145).

51.4.s.en: 2. A poem on seeking wisdom and establishing a school for teaching wisdom

51.4.0.en: 18 When I was yet young, before I went abroad, I desired wisdom openly in my prayer. 19 I prayed for her before the temple, and I will seek her out even to the end. And she flourished as a ripening grape. 20 My heart delighted in her, my foot went the right way, and from my youth up I sought after her. 21 I bowed down mine ear a little, and received her, 22 and found much learning for myself, and I had great profit therein. 23 He that giveth me wisdom, I will give glory to him, 24 for I purposed to do after her, and I was zealous of that which is good; and I shall not be confounded. 25 My soul hath wrestled with her, and in my doings I was exact. 26 I stretched forth my hands to the heaven above, and bewailed my ignorances of her. 27 I directed my soul unto her, and I found her in pureness. 28 With her I had my heart joined from the beginning; therefore shall I not be forsaken. 29 My heart was troubled in seeking her; therefore have I gotten a good possession. 30 The Lord hath given me a tongue for my reward, and I will praise him therewith. 31 Draw near unto me, ye unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning. 32 Wherefore are ye slow, and what say ye of these things, seeing your souls are very thirsty? 33 I opened my mouth, and said, Buy her for yourselves without money. 34 Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction: she is hard at hand to find. 35 Behold with your eyes, how that I have had but little labour, and have gotten unto me much rest. 36 Get learning with a great sum of money, and get much gold by her. 37 Let your soul rejoice in his mercy, and be not ashamed of his praise. 38 Work your work betimes, and in his time he will give you your reward.

51.4.1.en: He closed the book with a poem arranged according to the Hebrew alphabet, in which he praises wisdom, takes pride in her, seeks her, and also establishes a school for teaching her. This poem corresponds to the alphabetical poem at the end of the book of Proverbs, where Solomon praises the virtuous wife. Ben Sira looked upon wisdom as upon a holy wife, God's gift to His believers. Moreover, the book began with the seeking of wisdom from God, and he closed it with a positive, joyful thought.

51.4.2.en: The alphabetical arrangement of the poem enables the reader to memorize it easily by heart, and to count it as a personal poem of his own. It is as though what Ben Sira attained of success in his enjoyment of the divine wisdom is not a matter for him alone, but he desires every man to take pride in having attained it.

51.4.3.en: While I was still young and before the start of my journeys, I sought wisdom openly in my prayer [13].

51.4.4.en: If he has already spoken of the blessings of journeys for enjoying the good things of others, he affirms here that journeys alone are not enough; rather, while still a young man, before his travels in many lands, he used to pray openly, declaring his need of wisdom! For she is the fruit of prayers and supplications, so that the grace of God may work, and give him understanding to distinguish true experiences from corrupt ones.

51.4.5.en: Before the temple I prayed for her, and to the end of my life I will seek after her [14].

51.4.6.en: Since the divine wisdom lifts man up to the holy life, whenever he stood before the holy temple he asked the Holy One to give him wisdom. And whenever he received wisdom his heart was kindled with longing for more of it, and his heart remains so to the last moment of his life on earth! Thus he brings out here two matters of the utmost importance:

51.4.7.en: a. True wisdom, which is from God, cannot be separated from the holy life; therefore he seeks her in his chamber as he seeks her openly in the holy temple, without shame!

51.4.8.en: b. He feels that man, however great his wisdom, will never reach the perfection of wisdom, so he continues to seek her as long as he is in the body, until the day of his departure from the world.

51.4.9.en: My heart delighted in her blossom as in a grape that ripens. And my foot walked in her straight way, and from my youth I searched after her [15].

51.4.10.en: Ben Sira makes clear to his disciples, when they see what wisdom has poured out upon him of the joy of the Spirit, that it is not something new; rather, from his youth he came to know her and set out on her way and enjoyed, as it were, her flowers that are on their way to becoming ripe grapes. In this he urges his disciples, in a spirit of hope and joy, to begin the journey of wisdom, even if they have not yet enjoyed the ripe grapes, that is, the deep joy; they will attain it so long as they persevere on the way.

51.4.11.en: I inclined my ear a little and received her, and found much instruction for myself [16].

51.4.12.en: Here he calls his disciples to incline their ear to the voice of the Lord through the Law, that they may receive wisdom and grow in her through much unceasing instruction.

51.4.13.en: And I advanced by her grace; I glorify Him who gave me wisdom [17].

51.4.14.en: As he advanced in the knowledge of wisdom he did not become proud; rather, this knowledge kindled his heart with praise and the glorification of God.

51.4.15.en: For I resolved to practice wisdom, and I was zealous for the good, and was not ashamed [18].

51.4.16.en: His continual advance in the knowledge of wisdom drives him to be determined to practice her, not in slackness, but with sincere zeal and with pride in her, without being ashamed of her even if others criticize him.

51.5.0.en: My soul strove for her, and I examined myself firmly in fulfilling the Law. And I spread out my hands to the heights, and mourned for my ignorance of her [19].

51.5.1.en: He often links wisdom with the Law, and even with walking in it in earnestness and firmness, for fear of laxity in conduct through preoccupation with dry philosophical thoughts. This conduct is not achieved without God's help and the practice of repentance. For this reason he links his growth in wisdom with spreading out his hands to the heights and weeping over his ignorance and his sins.

51.6.0.en: I directed my soul to her, and in purity I found her, and for her sake I gained a heart from the beginning, therefore I shall not be forsaken [20].

51.6.1.en: He links the continual enjoyment of wisdom with purity of hands and heart, that is, purity of conduct and work together with purity of heart and thought.

51.7.0.en: My heart was stirred in seeking her, therefore I gained a good possession [21].

51.7.1.en: He affirms that when he speaks of purity of heart, he means the stirring of his whole being to enjoy holiness and to seek wisdom; therefore he counted her possession a great reward.

51.8.0.en: The Lord gave me a tongue as a reward, and with it I praise Him [22].

51.8.1.en: "The tongue" here means the ability even to express what is in his heart of sweetness and longing to praise the Lord. This ability is a divine gift and a talent that must be kindled.

51.9.0.en: Draw near to me, you who are unlearned, and dwell in my school [23].

51.9.1.en: The word "my school" came as "beth hamidrash," or the house of learning, where Ben Sira used to gather with his disciples as the people of his house, or his family beloved to him. What Ben Sira did is a shadow of the work of the Lord Christ, who chose His disciples who clung to Him.

51.9.2.en: Schools were attached to the synagogues; and some leaders demanded that there be a school in every village, and every child was obliged to enroll in it, and learning was not separated from worship and the godly life.

51.9.3.en: The writer lived interacting with all classes, entering deeply into what is for the edification of men according to their various particular circumstances.

51.9.4.en: v The word of God has been addressed to us. It was declared in order to counsel us, and as the Holy Scripture says: "Receive instruction in the house of instruction." Instruction is given so that we may learn, and the school of instruction is the Church of Christ.

51.9.5.en: Let us ask ourselves what the purpose and aim of this instruction is: who is it that learns, and who is it that gives the instruction. One learns in order to live well, and the aim of his learning to live well is that he may live eternally. Christians learn with this goal, and the One who teaches is Christ[2].

51.10.0.en: St. Augustine: Why do you say that you are in need of these things, and that your souls are very thirsty? [24]

51.10.1.en: Ben Sira asks how long the thirst of his disciples has lasted; let them then come forward in a spirit of prayer and drink, for God is ready to give them wisdom. And as it is written in the book of Proverbs: "Come, eat of my bread, and drink of the wine which I have mingled. Forsake the foolish, and live; and go in the way of understanding" (Prov 9:5-6).

51.10.2.en: I opened my mouth and spoke: Acquire wisdom for yourselves without price[3] [25].

51.10.3.en: Ben Sira affirms to his disciples that they are without excuse, for wisdom is not sold for silver, presenting himself as an example, that he opened his mouth with sincere zeal, longing and faith, and so attained her.

51.10.4.en: Teaching in the Jewish tradition was free of charge, and the rabbis who taught in the schools depended for their living on other means, and at a later time they worked in trade[4]. It is stated in the Mishnah: "If you learn much in the Law, you will receive a great reward, and the One who is committed to this task (God) is faithful to give you the reward of your work[5]."

51.11.0.en: Put your neck under her yoke, and let your souls receive her instruction. She is near, so you will find her [26].

51.11.1.en: Wisdom does not depart from the one who has enjoyed her, but accompanies him in the grave, and rescues him from the claws of Hades. She is near to us, because Christ, the Wisdom of God, establishes His kingdom within us (Lk 17:21).

51.12.0.en: See with your eyes how I labored a little and found much rest for myself [27].

51.12.1.en: He urges the reader to submit to the yoke of wisdom, for he himself has experienced great rest under this yoke.

51.12.2.en: v He who is plunged into countless struggles for the sake of virtue, and attains to her, and accomplishes still more labors, lives to the end like Lazarus, who toiled in many sorrows (Lk 16), and like Job, who was engaged in struggles against the enemy. He says: "Those who are engaged in toil are at rest (see Job 3:17). Therefore the Lord called those who labor and are heavy laden to rest (Mt 11:28).

51.12.3.en: Now how can it be said of those who labor in good works that they are heavy laden? Because: "They that go forth weeping, bearing seed for sowing, shall come again with rejoicing, bringing their sheaves with them" (Ps 126:6), full of the fruits that have returned to them from their sowing of the seed. Therefore those are said to be heavy laden who have sowed bountifully and reaped bountifully (2 Cor 9:6), and with eternal joy cast the sheaves of spiritual fruit upon their shoulders. So then, he who is saved by God, to whom He offers redemption, labors in this life, and after this lives to the end. He does not see corruption when he sees the wise die.

51.12.4.en: He who chooses the narrow and afflicted way instead of the wide and broad one: in the time of God's visitation, when those who did not believe the words of God, but walked after the desires of their vain hearts, are cast into eternal punishment, I say that he does not see eternal destruction, perpetual misery. But he says in truth that the wise have been trained in craftiness. And Jeremiah says concerning them: "They are wise to do evil, but to do good they have no knowledge" (Jer 4:22). As it is also said: "Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools" (Rom 1:22). "For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God" (1 Cor 3:19).

51.12.5.en: And because this wisdom makes men fools, God says that He will destroy the wisdom of the wise and bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent. Therefore these false beliefs, which are called knowledge, bring death to those who receive them. But this death is not seen by those who are saved by Him, who is pleased to save those who trust in the foolishness of His proclamation[6].

51.13.0.en: St. Basil the Great: Acquire instruction with a great sum of silver, and by it you will gain much gold [28].

51.13.1.en: In verse 25 he speaks of material silver, for wisdom is not sold for money. But here he speaks of it as instruction by the Law, of which it was said: "The words of the Lord are pure words, as silver tried in a furnace" (Ps 12:6). As for the reward, it is the gaining of much gold. This gold points to the pledge of the heavenly life.

51.14.0.en: Let your souls rejoice in His mercy, and be not ashamed of praising Him [29].

51.15.0.en: Do your work before the appointed time, and He will reward you in His appointed time [30].

51.15.1.en: He closes the poem, indeed the whole book, with the thought that whoever earnestly strives to obtain true wisdom enjoys a pledge of heaven, so his soul rejoices in the mercies of God, and he is not ashamed to praise Him without ceasing. As for his reward, it is in the great day of the Lord, when he will enjoy the fellowship of eternal glory, and see God face to face.

51.16.s.en: Let me offer You the sacrifice of continual thanksgiving, O Giver of wisdom!

51.16.0.en: v What shall I ask of You, O incarnate Wisdom of God?

51.16.1.en: Sanctify my heart and my life, that I may be made worthy of Your free grace!

51.16.2.en: I praise You in every state, for every state, and in all states, for You are the secret of the joy of my heart, and You sanctify all my life.

51.16.3.en: v May You accompany me on the journey of my life, so that my heart does not cease to praise You.

51.16.4.en: My soul thirsts for You, and I hunger for Your wisdom.

51.16.5.en: May You lift my heart to Your heavens, and pour Your splendor into my depths.

51.16.6.en: Take me to Your glories day by day!

51.16.7.en: Until I see You face to face!
